claims.text: UN News (23 October 2026), citing the UN Human Rights Office (OHCHR) and High Commissioner Volker Türk: drone strikes "killed at least 306 people and injured hundreds more in the first three weeks of October alone." OHCHR documented strikes on displacement shelters, a gold-mining site, a transport convoy and a market across West Kordofan, Blue Nile and Abyei.

UN News (21 October 2026): nearly two dozen countries held the sixth round of Consultative Meetings on Enhancing Coordination of Peace Initiatives and Efforts in Sudan in Geneva, co-hosted by Switzerland and the UN; neither the Sudanese government nor the RSF attended, as the meeting is for mediators to coordinate. The UN Secretary-General's Personal Envoy Pekka Haavisto separately planned to meet the 'Quad' (US, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt) and the 'Quintet' (African Union, IGAD, UN, EU, League of Arab States); delegates discussed building confidence toward a comprehensive ceasefire and a Sudanese-led transitional political process, but the article reports no ceasefire agreement or other concrete outcome.

UN News (5 November 2026): UN peacekeeping chief Jean-Pierre Lacroix told the Security Council that the 19 October 2026 drone strikes in Abyei killed at least 30 people and injured about 59, with peacekeepers still checking whether the toll is an underestimate; he called the attacks the first of their kind in Abyei, adding 'a new and concerning dimension' to the area's security, and the strikes set off major fires and forced dozens of civilians from their homes. The UN's Special Envoy, Guang Cong, called the strikes one of the deadliest incidents in Abyei's history.

UN News (10 November 2026), citing UNICEF spokesperson James Elder at a Geneva briefing: 'This year in Sudan, two in three child casualties were killed by armed drones,' and 'not a single day passed without a drone strike on a power station in Sudan' -- up to 15 power stations were hit in October 2026 alone. Elder said UNICEF's Sudan response is just one-third funded and described meeting a teenage drone-attack victim from El Obeid, where Human Rights Council investigators say civilians live in constant fear of drone attack; the article gives no new West Kordofan-, Blue Nile- or Abyei-specific casualty figures.

UN News (23 October 2026), per OHCHR documentation: alleged drone strikes attributed to government forces on displacement shelters in Ghubeish and El Nuhud, West Kordofan, between 6 and 10 October 2026, killed at least 25 civilians.

UN News (23 October 2026), per OHCHR documentation: an alleged RSF drone strike on 9 October 2026 on displaced people mining gold at Abu Shendi, Blue Nile, killed at least 31 people, most of them women and children.
UN News (23 October 2026), per OHCHR documentation: a repeat ('double tap') drone strike on a transport truck at Dibab, West Kordofan, on 18 October 2026, killed at least 139 people.

UN News (23 October 2026): a 19 October 2026 strike on Amiet Market and Todach, Abyei, killed more than 80 people, per UN peacekeepers (UNISFA) who visited the affected communities; UNISFA's Acting Force Commander, Brigadier General Adebowale Ajabge, said the mission's hospital in Todach treated more than 27 injured people, and the Security Council said the toll is expected to rise.

UN News (19 October 2026): UN Spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said the UN is 'alarmed by the continued deadly drone strikes' killing civilians, including children, across Sudan. That Monday, drone strikes injured at least 19 people in a busy market in Abyei, and a strike near Khartoum airport reportedly killed one civilian and led to flight cancellations; over the preceding weekend, drone attacks in West Darfur, South Darfur and North Kordofan reportedly killed at least 19 people, including 10 children. The article also reports that 25 Sudanese Red Crescent volunteers have been killed since the conflict began, including one killed the preceding week in Um Darfa, Blue Nile State, while providing first aid after a drone attack on a health centre; Sudan's humanitarian response plan is just over 43 percent funded.

UN News (29 October 2026), citing UNICEF: at least five children were killed and two injured in a drone attack on a market in Nyala, South Darfur, on Monday 27 October 2026; the victims were three boys and two girls aged seven to 14. UNICEF said more than 400 children were killed or injured in Sudan from January to September 2026, with armed drone attacks causing a significant share. UNICEF's Etleva Kadilli said: 'The killing and injuring of children must end.'

UN News (3 November 2026), citing UN Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator for Sudan Denise Brown: drone strikes on power stations and fuel depots have cut electricity to a hospital just outside Khartoum, halting dialysis for 25 patients; fuel queues in Khartoum now stretch for kilometres and hundreds of aid trucks are stranded for lack of fuel. Brown said the World Food Programme has had seven aid-convoy hits this year (and 20 over the past two years), and said: "This is not about politics. This is about people," adding there is "no defence for repeatedly hitting power stations and fuel stations."

UN News (5 November 2026), citing local sources relayed in the same report on UN peacekeeping chief Jean-Pierre Lacroix's Security Council briefing: a drone strike hit an electricity transmission station and the Ar Rusayris Dam at Ed Damazine, causing widespread blackouts, and a strike on a residential area the same day killed two civilians; an airstrike on Um Bader the same day killed two women, injured ten people and damaged two water stations.

description: Drone strikes have hit displacement shelters, a gold-mining site, a transport convoy, markets and power infrastructure across West Kordofan, Blue Nile, Abyei, South Darfur and Khartoum state, Sudan, since October 2026, killing hundreds of civilians. The UN Human Rights Office documented at least 306 killed and hundreds more injured in the first three weeks of October alone, including strikes in Ghubeish/El Nuhud (25 dead), Abu Shendi (31 dead) and Dibab (139 dead); UN peacekeeping chief Jean-Pierre Lacroix told the Security Council on 5 November that the 19 October Abyei strikes, the first of their kind there, killed at least 30 and injured about 59. Strikes on power and fuel infrastructure now also cripple hospitals and aid logistics, including a dialysis-halting outage near Khartoum and blackouts from strikes on Ed Damazine's grid and the Ar Rusayris Dam; UNICEF said on 10 November that up to 15 power stations nationwide were hit in October alone and that two in three child casualties this year were caused by armed drones. Geneva peace talks on 21 October produced no ceasefire. This surge is distinct from the separate siege of El Obeid in North Kordofan.

impact.summary: The UN Human Rights Office documented at least 306 civilians killed and hundreds more injured by drone strikes across Sudan in the first three weeks of October 2026 alone, including 25 dead in Ghubeish/El Nuhud (West Kordofan), 31 dead in Abu Shendi (Blue Nile) and 139 dead in Dibab (West Kordofan). UN peacekeeping chief Jean-Pierre Lacroix told the Security Council on 5 November that the 19 October Abyei strikes -- the first of their kind there -- killed at least 30 and injured about 59. UNICEF reported a 27 October strike on a market in Nyala, South Darfur, killed five children. Strikes on power and fuel infrastructure continue to cripple the response: a hospital outside Khartoum halted dialysis, a strike on Ed Damazine's electricity station and the Ar Rusayris Dam caused blackouts, and an Um Bader airstrike killed two women and damaged two water stations. UNICEF said on 10 November that up to 15 power stations nationwide were struck in October alone and two in three child casualties this year were caused by armed drones. Geneva peace talks on 21 October produced no ceasefire.

updates.text: UNICEF spokesperson James Elder said up to 15 power stations nationwide were struck by drones in October alone -- 'not a single day passed without a drone strike on a power station in Sudan' -- and that two in three child casualties in Sudan this year were caused by armed drones; UNICEF's Sudan response is only one-third funded.

UN peacekeeping chief Lacroix told the Security Council the 19 October Abyei drone strikes, the first of their kind there, killed at least 30 and injured about 59; peacekeepers are checking if the toll is an underestimate. Strikes also hit Ed Damazine's power grid/dam and Um Bader (2 women killed). Separately, ~24 countries held Geneva peace talks on 21 October; no ceasefire resulted.

UN Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator Denise Brown said strikes on power and fuel infrastructure have halted dialysis for 25 patients at a hospital outside Khartoum and stranded hundreds of aid trucks for lack of fuel; WFP has had seven aid-convoy hits this year. Brown: "This is not about politics. This is about people."

UNICEF reported a drone strike on a market in Nyala, South Darfur, killed five children (three boys, two girls, aged 7-14) and injured two more; UNICEF said more than 400 children had been killed or injured by Sudan's conflict, drone attacks a significant share, between January and September 2026.

The UN condemned a further wave of drone strikes across Sudan: an Abyei market strike injured at least 19 people and a strike near Khartoum airport killed one civilian, on top of at least 19 people (including 10 children) killed over the preceding weekend in West Darfur, South Darfur and North Kordofan. Separately, 25 Sudanese Red Crescent volunteers have been killed since the conflict began.
